findings.consequence: The component carries a second modal state value that is not rendered or passed to the dialog, so future changes can make `article` and `articleHtml` drift without changing any user-visible data needs.
findings.evidence: `article` is declared at line 17, but the template passes only `articleHtml` and `modalOpen` to `ReaderDictionaryDialog`; `article` is otherwise only used as a boolean companion to non-empty sanitized HTML.
findings.recommendation: Remove `article`, compute `modalOpen` from `articleHtml.value.length > 0`, and let successful lookup assign only sanitized HTML after the generated response type has been accepted.
